```{r setup, include = FALSE}
# HTML figures are drawn as PNG and kept as WebP: lossless, or lossy at quality 90 when that is less than half the
# size. The PDF figures stay vector graphics. Any failure of magick (not installed, no WebP, or a broken
# installation whose system libraries are missing) keeps the PNG
webp <- function(path) {
  if (knitr::is_latex_output() || !grepl(pattern = "[.]png$", x = path)) return(path)
  tryCatch(
      {
        if (!requireNamespace("magick", quietly = TRUE) || !isTRUE(magick::magick_config()$webp)) return(path)
        img <- magick::image_read(path)
        out <- sub(pattern = "[.]png$", replacement = ".webp", x = path)
        tmp <- tempfile(fileext = ".webp")
        magick::image_write(
            image   = img
          , path    = out
          , format  = "webp"
          , quality = 100
          , defines = c(`webp:lossless` = "true")
          )
        magick::image_write(image = img, path = tmp, format = "webp", quality = 90)
        if (file.size(tmp) < file.size(out) / 2) file.copy(from = tmp, to = out, overwrite = TRUE)
        unlink(c(path, tmp))
        out
      }
    , error = function(e) path
    )
}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = FALSE, comment = "", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.2,
                      dev = if (knitr::is_latex_output()) "cairo_pdf" else "ragg_png", dpi = 96,
                      fig.process = webp)
if (requireNamespace("VetResearchLMM", quietly = TRUE)) library(VetResearchLMM) else
  pkgload::load_all(export_all = FALSE, helpers = FALSE, quiet = TRUE)
```


# Abstract

Chapter 3 of the book applies the mixed model to a designed experiment with a covariate (Example 3.1), to the
estimation of heritability and breeding values (Example 3.2) and to repeated measures with several covariance
structures (Example 3.3). The book prints only part of the data of Examples 3.1 and 3.2, so their analyses run but
cannot reproduce the printed numbers; the complete data of Example 3.3 reproduce every printed number.

```{r ref}
ref <-
  vlm_reference(
      source   = "Example 3"
    , evaluate = TRUE
    , level    = 1
    )
```

# Example 3.1: doses nested in drug, with a covariate

```{r}
m1 <-
  vlm_fit(
      fixed    = PCV2 ~ drug + drug:dose
    , data     = ex31
    , random   = ~ drug:herd
    , repeated = NULL
    , method   = c("REML", "ML", "Type3")
    , ddfm     = "satterth"
    , type     = 3
    , class    = c("herd", "dose")
    , bound    = TRUE
    , control  = list()
    )
m1$tests
vlm_estimate(
    fit    = m1
  , L      = list(
        "Mean Samorin"         = list(Intercept = 1, drug = c(0, 1), "drug:dose" = c(0, 0, 1))
      , "Berenil 2 doses"      = list("drug:dose" = c(1, -1, 0))
      , "Ber vs Sam at dose 1" = list(drug = c(1, -1), "drug:dose" = c(1, 0, -1))
      )
  , random = NULL
  , level  = 0.95
  )
```

Model 3 lets each treatment have its own slope on the PCV at treatment, and compares the treatments for an animal
with PCV1 = 18:

```{r}
m3 <-
  vlm_fit(
      fixed    = PCV2 ~ drug + drug:dose + PCV1:drug:dose
    , data     = ex31
    , random   = ~ drug:herd
    , repeated = NULL
    , method   = c("REML", "ML", "Type3")
    , ddfm     = "kr"
    , type     = 3
    , class    = c("herd", "dose")
    , bound    = TRUE
    , control  = list()
    )
vlm_lsmeans(
    fit    = m3
  , specs  = ~ drug:dose
  , at     = list(PCV1 = 18)
  , diff   = FALSE
  , adjust = c("none", "tukey", "bonferroni", "sidak")
  , level  = 0.95
  )
```

# Example 3.2: heritability and sire predictions

```{r}
f32 <-
  vlm_fit(
      fixed    = Ww ~ sex + agew + breed
    , data     = ex32
    , random   = ~ breed:sire_id
    , repeated = NULL
    , method   = c("REML", "ML", "Type3")
    , ddfm     = "satterth"
    , type     = 3
    , class    = "breed"
    , bound    = TRUE
    , control  = list()
    )
f32$covariance
vlm_lsmeans(
    fit    = f32
  , specs  = ~ breed
  , at     = NULL
  , diff   = TRUE
  , adjust = "tukey"
  , level  = 0.95
  )$lsmeans
```

On this part of the data the sire variance is estimated as zero, so the heritability $h^2 = 4\sigma_s^2/
(\sigma_s^2 + \sigma^2)$ is zero; with the complete data the book finds 0.49.

# Example 3.3: covariance structures for repeated measures

Model 1 (a random animal effect, equivalently compound symmetry), Model 2 (first-order autoregressive errors) and
Model 3 (a random intercept and slope per animal):

```{r}
cs <-
  vlm_fit(
      fixed    = PCV ~ breed + breed:time
    , data     = ex33
    , random   = NULL
    , repeated = vlm_repeated(
          type    = c("vc", "cs", "ar1", "sp_pow", "un")[2]
        , subject = ~ animal_id:breed
        , order   = NULL
        )
    , method   = c("REML", "ML", "Type3")
    , ddfm     = c("default", "contain", "residual", "betwithin", "satterth", "kr")
    , type     = 3
    , class    = NULL
    , bound    = TRUE
    , control  = list()
    )
ar <-
  vlm_fit(
      fixed    = PCV ~ breed + breed:time
    , data     = ex33
    , random   = NULL
    , repeated = vlm_repeated(
          type    = c("vc", "cs", "ar1", "sp_pow", "un")[3]
        , subject = ~ animal_id:breed
        , order   = NULL
        )
    , method   = c("REML", "ML", "Type3")
    , ddfm     = c("default", "contain", "residual", "betwithin", "satterth", "kr")
    , type     = 3
    , class    = NULL
    , bound    = TRUE
    , control  = list()
    )
rc <-
  vlm_fit(
      fixed    = PCV ~ breed + breed:time
    , data     = ex33
    , random   = vlm_random(
          effects = ~ 1 + time
        , subject = ~ animal_id:breed
        , type    = c("vc", "un")[2]
        )
    , repeated = NULL
    , method   = c("REML", "ML", "Type3")
    , ddfm     = c("default", "contain", "residual", "betwithin", "satterth", "kr")
    , type     = 3
    , class    = NULL
    , bound    = TRUE
    , control  = list()
    )
rc$covariance
cmp <-
  vlm_compare(
      CS   = cs
    , AR1  = ar
    , RC   = rc
    , test = TRUE
    )
cmp
plot(cmp)
```

The book compared Models 1 and 2 only (the restricted log-likelihoods $-391.73$ and $-396.57$ favour compound
symmetry); the random coefficients model has a much smaller AIC still, as the negative covariance of the intercepts
and slopes (animals that start higher fall faster) suggests.
